title: Enterprise Onboarding, Health Checks, QBRs and Escalation Playbook
author: Priya Natarajan
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended playbooks and artifacts for enterprise onboarding, ongoing health checks, quarterly business reviews (QBRs), and the escalation process. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support Engineers, and SREs who collaborate to deliver predictable, high-quality onboarding and operational support for enterprise customers.

Scope

- Onboarding flow and checklist for new enterprise customers (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- Escalation playbook including severity definitions, routing, and SLAs.
- Integration guidance summary and common troubleshooting commands.
- Known issues, mitigations and temporary workarounds.
- Health check cadence, automated checks, and QBR artifacts and templates.

1) Enterprise Onboarding Checklist (high level)

Pre-sales -> Kickoff
1. Create shared onboarding space and invite stakeholders (SE, CS, Customer PM, Security).
2. Confirm deployment mode and contract (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private).
3. Share architecture questionnaire and collect answers. Key fields: expected TPS, average sequence length, P95 latency target, data residency, compliance needs.

Week 0: Provisioning & Access
- Hosted: Issue API keys, create dedicated project, enable usage alerts.
- Dedicated/Private: Confirm capacity reservation, network allowlist, KMS/HSM configuration.
- Assign primary CS owner and SE.

Week 1: Integration & Validation
- Provide SDK quickstart and sample routes.
- Run baseline perf tests using customer's representative prompt sets (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).
- Validate auth, tracing headers, and request/response schemas.

Week 2: Performance Tuning & Quality Gates
- Apply batching and cache settings recommended by Redwood Optimize.
- Run evals on representative prompts; confirm quality thresholds are met.
- Configure monitoring dashboards and alerting (cost, latency, error rate).

Go-live & Handover
- Cutover plan and canary rollout for critical routes.
- Hand off runbooks and escalation contacts.
- Schedule first 30/60/90 day health check meetings.

2) Escalation Playbook

Severity definitions and target response/resolution times
- P0 (Critical): Complete outage or catastrophic data loss. CS/SE & SRE notified immediately. Response: 15 minutes. Target resolution: 4 hours (exec update at 60 minutes).
- P1 (High): Significant customer-impacting degradation (p95 latency > 2x SLO, or error rate > 5%). Response: 30 minutes. Target resolution: 8 hours.
- P2 (Medium): Functional impairment for a subset of features or customers. Response: 4 hours. Target resolution: 3 business days.
- P3 (Low): Minor issues, feature requests, doc inaccuracies. Response: 48 hours. Target resolution: 10 business days.

Escalation routing
- Level 1: Support Engineers (triage, logs, reproduce).
- Level 2: SE/CS (integration issues, contract/configuration).
- Level 3: SRE / Runtime engineers (performance, kernel, capacity).
- Level 4: Engineering leads / Execs (product defects, contractual SLA breaches).

Steps to escalate (numbered procedure)
1. Open ticket in Zendesk with severity and all required fields (see ticket template below).
2. Attach logs, sample request IDs, timestamps, and trace IDs.
3. Run standard diagnostic runbook (latency profiling, tail sampling, KV cache inspection).
4. If unresolved within response SLA, escalate to next level and notify customer with status update.
5. For P0/P1, initiate conference bridge and mark ticket as incident in incident tracker.

Ticket template (YAML)
- ticket_id: <auto-generated>
- title: Support: <short problem statement>
- severity: P0|P1|P2|P3
- customer: <customer-name>
- impacted_routes: [ /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings ]
- first_detected: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
- observed_metrics: >
    p50_latency_ms: 45
    p95_latency_ms: 870
    error_rate_pct: 6.2
- attached_artifacts: [logs.tar.gz, trace-12345, config.yaml]

3) Integration guide (common checks and commands)

Authentication and basic API check
- Confirm API key is present and project-level quotas are not exhausted.
- Quick sanity curl (replace API_KEY and ENDPOINT):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}' | jq
```

Tracing and request attribution
- Ensure client provides headers: x-rw-request-id, x-rw-customer-id. These are required for log lookups and billing reconciliation.

Performance debugging checklist
- Collect sample request IDs and correlate with request traces.
- Check route-level SLO dashboard for spikes in p95 latency and error counts.
- For Dedicated/Private: verify GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, and batch sizes.

4) Known issues and workarounds (living list)

- Issue: Intermittent high p95 latency on long sequences (>1024 tokens) on older quantized variants.
  - Symptom: p95 spikes when batch composition has many long sequences.
  - Mitigation: Use model variant optimized for long sequences (model-name-longseq-v2) and enable per-request max_tokens cap. For immediate relief, enable strict batching_policy: fairness_mode: true.

- Issue: Embeddings throughput drop under high concurrent small requests.
  - Mitigation: Recommend client-side batching (send multiple texts in one call) or enable server-side micro-batching via route config: 

  batching_config:
    max_batch_size: 256
    max_wait_ms: 25

- Issue: OAuth KMS key rotation caused transient auth failures in Private deployments.
  - Mitigation: Roll forward new key with dual-key acceptance window; if unavailable, fallback to cached short-lived token for up to 10 minutes while rotation is completed.

Each known issue entry should include owner (team), tags, and ticket references. Maintain this section as a table in the customer's onboarding space when applicable.

5) Health checks and QBR materials

Health check cadence and automated checks
- 7-day automated health report: p50/p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hit rate, request distribution by route. Generated by CS tooling and emailed to customer and internal owners.
- 30/60/90 day manual check: integration items, rolling quality evaluation, cost optimization opportunities.

QBR template (30-45 minutes)
- Agenda:
  1. Executive summary (5 min): key wins and open risks.
  2. Usage & cost trends (10 min): tokens, embeddings, unit cost, anomalies.
  3. Reliability & performance (10 min): SLO adherence, incidents since last QBR, mitigations.
  4. Product roadmap & upcoming changes (5 min): deprecations, new model variants, runtime improvements.
  5. Action items & next steps (5-10 min): owner, due date.

QBR deliverables
- Slide deck (PDF) with charts exported from Redwood Console dashboards.
- Action log in CS workspace and follow-up meeting scheduled.

6) Ownership, escalation contacts and SLAs

Primary contacts
- CS Owner: Priya Natarajan (priya@redwood.ai)
- Solutions Engineer: Liam O'Neill (liam@redwood.ai)
- Support Pager: support-pager@redwood.ai (monitored 24/7)
- SRE On-call: see /confluence/eng-sre/rota for current on-call

SLA reminders
- Hosted: 99.9% uptime, latency targets defined per-tier in contract.
- Dedicated: SLA per contract, include committed slots and burst policies.
- Private: SLAs are contract-specific; CS should coordinate with security and infra owners for on-prem gate checks.

7) Post-incident and continuous improvement

- Every P0/P1 incident requires a postmortem within 7 calendar days. The postmortem must link to the original ticket, timeline of events, root cause analysis, and action items with owners.
- Track recurring issues in the regression-triage board and prioritize engineering work through the model-serving-standards ADRs.

Appendices

A: Diagnostic runbook quick commands
- Export traces for a request id: `rwctl traces export --request-id <id> --output traces.tar.gz`
- Generate 7-day health report: `cs-tooling generate-health --customer <cust> --days 7 --out report.pdf`

B: QBR slide checklist
- Cover slide, Executive summary, Trend charts (tokens, cost), Incident summary, Optimization opportunities, Action log.

C: Related resources
- Integration playbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-integration-playbook-2026
- Incident process: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Performance standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards

Document maintenance
- Owner: customer-success team. Review cadence: quarterly or after any P0 incident.

For questions or suggested changes, open an internal PR in the CS handbook repo or contact the owner listed above.
